What we do

Our services

Your first visit

What to expect

Seeing a new health professional can feel daunting. Here's how your first appointment works.

Before you come

Bring your Medicare card, any referral or care plan, NDIS or package details, a list of your medications and any scans or reports.

During the appointment

Your therapist will ask about your health and goals, carry out a gentle assessment and explain what they find in plain language.

Your plan

Together you'll agree on a treatment plan, how often to come and exercises or strategies to use at home.

After your visit

With your consent, we send a summary to your GP or coordinator so everyone involved in your care is on the same page.

Bringing a family member, carer or support person is always welcome. Let us know if you need an interpreter.

Home / About us

About Rapha Allied Health

Rapha is a Melbourne allied health practice. We see clients in our clinics, in their homes and in schools, and we work closely with GPs, support coordinators and families so everyone is working toward the same goals.

Our mission

Integrated, person-centred care

To deliver integrated, person-centred care through skilled professionals, supporting our clients' physical, emotional and social wellbeing with collaborative and culturally sensitive services.

Our vision

Compassionate, evidence-based care

To provide compassionate, holistic and evidence-based allied health care that helps every person reach their optimal wellbeing.

How we work

Goals you set

Therapy starts with what matters to you: getting back to work, walking to the shops, talking with friends or staying safely at home.

One team around you

Physiotherapists, occupational therapists, speech therapists and exercise physiologists share notes and plan together.

Care where you are

Our mobile service covers all of Melbourne, so you can be seen at home when travelling to a clinic is hard.

Clear communication

We send timely reports to your GP, plan manager or care coordinator, written in plain language.

Acknowledgement of Country

Rapha Allied Health acknowledges Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples as the traditional custodians of the lands where we live, learn and work. We pay our respects to Elders past and present.

Home / Our story
Our story

Three decades of experience. A thirst to make a difference.

Rapha Allied Health grew from thirty years of caring for people in hospitals, clinics and homes, and from a simple, stubborn belief that health care could be better.

“We saw people waiting too long, travelling too far and falling through the gaps between services. Rapha exists so that every person can get skilled, compassionate care that helps them heal, live well and stay independent.”

The Rapha Allied Health team
The journey

Our journey

  1. Three decades

    Experience that shaped us

    Rapha was built on three decades of allied health experience across hospitals, primary care, orthopaedic and pain clinics, community and home-based care, and clinical teaching. That time showed us what works when care is skilled, timely and joined up, and what happens to people when it is not.

  2. The thirst

    A thirst to make a difference

    Experience alone was never enough. What drove Rapha was a thirst to make a real difference: to shorten waits, bring therapy to people who cannot easily travel, and make sure nobody falls between GP, hospital, NDIS and aged care services.

  3. The name

    “Rapha” means to heal

    The word rapha means “to heal” or “to restore”. It captures what we want for every client: not only treating a condition, but restoring confidence, independence and hope.

  4. Mobile at heart

    Taking care to people

    From the start, Rapha was designed to be mobile. Too many people miss out on therapy because they cannot drive, are recovering from surgery, live with disability or care for someone at home. So our clinicians travel to them: to homes, schools, workplaces and aged care residences. We also work inside local medical centres alongside GPs, so care is joined up wherever a person is seen.

  5. Growing together

    More places, more people, more care

    Today our mobile team visits homes in every part of Melbourne, from the CBD to the Mornington Peninsula, Werribee and the Yarra Ranges, and our clinicians also consult at Doctors on Clyde in Clyde North, Narre Warren Medical Centre and Dandenong Doctors. Our team spans physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech pathology and exercise physiology, supporting NDIS participants, older Australians, veterans, GP patients and private clients.

Where we are heading

From Melbourne to the whole country

The vision has always been bigger than one suburb. Our goal is an allied health network that makes a difference for communities right across Australia.

Mobile care in every community

Taking our mobile model to more homes, GP clinics and aged care settings, in cities, regional towns and rural communities where access is hardest.

Reaching further with telehealth

Using telehealth alongside face-to-face care so distance is never the reason someone misses out.

Growing the next generation

Mentoring graduate clinicians and sharing three decades of clinical knowledge with the next generation.

Partnering for better outcomes

Working with GPs, hospitals, NDIS and aged care providers so care is joined up and nobody falls through the gaps.

Our values

What guides us

  • Compassion: every person treated with dignity and respect
  • Excellence: skilled, evidence-based care
  • Access: care that comes to you
  • Partnership: working with families, GPs and providers
  • Integrity: honest advice and clear communication

Be part of the journey

We accept a range of funding types. If you're unsure what you're eligible for, send us a referral or enquiry and we'll help you work it out.

Funding typeWho it's forReferral needed?What to know
NDISNDIS participantsNo. Self-referral welcomeWe work with plan-managed and self-managed participants. Share your NDIS number and plan dates on the referral.
Support at Home
formerly Home Care Packages		Older Australians with Support at Home funding, including transitioned Home Care Package clientsVia your provider or care partnerServices must match your approved classification and are invoiced to your provider.
Medicare (GP plan)People with a chronic condition managed by their GPYes, a GP chronic condition management plan (GPCCMP) and GP referralUp to 5 Medicare-rebated allied health services per calendar year. We do not bulk bill, so a gap fee applies.
DVAVeterans with a Gold, White or TPI Gold CardYes, from the usual GP (or specialist / discharge planner for an initial cycle)Each referral covers a treatment cycle of 12 sessions or 1 year, whichever ends first.

formerly STRC		Older people on Support at Home's short-term restorative pathwayVia your provider or care partnerTime-limited, goal-focused therapy at home.

Home / Patient information

Patient information

Your rights as a patient and how to get support.

Australian Charter of Healthcare Rights

Your rights as a patient

We follow the Australian Charter of Healthcare Rights. When you receive care from Rapha you have the right to:

AccessHealthcare services and treatment that meet your needs.
SafetySafe, high-quality care in a safe environment.
RespectBe treated as an individual, with dignity, and have your culture, identity, beliefs and choices recognised.
PartnershipAsk questions, be involved in open and honest communication, and make decisions about your care.
InformationClear information about your condition, the possible benefits and risks of treatment, and costs.
PrivacyHave your personal and health information kept secure and confidential.
Give feedbackProvide feedback without it affecting the way you are treated.

Interpreters

Free interpreting is available through TIS National on 131 450. Tell us your preferred language when you book and we'll arrange it.

Accessibility

Home visits are available if travelling is difficult. Use the A+ button at the top of the page for larger text.

Support people

You're welcome to bring a family member, carer or support person to any appointment.

Cancellations

If you can't make it, please let us know as early as possible so we can offer the time to someone else. Cancellation terms are in your service agreement.

Home / Privacy policy

Privacy policy

Rapha Allied Health handles personal and health information in line with the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth), the Australian Privacy Principles and the Health Records Act 2001 (Vic).

What we collect

Contact details, date of birth, emergency contacts, funding details (such as NDIS or Medicare information) and the health information needed to assess and treat you.

How we use it

To provide therapy, communicate with you and your treating team, send reports to referrers you have authorised, and bill funding bodies.

Who we share it with

Only with your consent, or where the law requires or permits it, for example your GP, plan manager, package provider or a funding body.

Storage and security

Records are kept in secure clinical systems with access limited to staff who need it, and retained for the periods required by Victorian law.

Access and correction

You can ask to see or correct your information at any time by emailing info@raphaalliedhealth.com.

Complaints

Contact us first so we can resolve your concern. If you're not satisfied, you can contact the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner or the Victorian Health Complaints Commissioner.
